answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a token bond and complete a randomly assigned, time-limited task whose result is checked against a hidden test. If one operator submits copied or invalid proofs across identities, those bonds are slashed. A sparrow can join cheaply, but a Sybil attacker must fund many bonds and spend labor completing distinct tasks; a real voyage can supply a verifiable task, making it costly to forge identities at scale.
